headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance mismatch: Notion AI’s workspace access plus RD-Agent’s broad API egress can expose shared content to third-party model providers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and databases, while RD-Agent can ingest files/logs and run browser/API workflows. If Notion content is copied into RD-Agent inputs, prompt injection can cross the boundary. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation between their shared workspace-style data flows.
conditions: IF Notion page content is manually or programmatically copied into RD-Agent prompts or files, injection becomes reachable.
IF RD-Agent treats imported text or logs as instructions, malicious workspace content can steer its outputs.
mitigations: Restrict transfers to plain-text excerpts with explicit quoting.
Add a human review step before RD-Agent consumes Notion-derived content.
Use a fixed prompt template that labels imported text as untrusted.
Separate shared workspace content from agent input folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor-hosted backend calls downstream model providers. RD-Agent handles financial reports, papers, datasets, logs, and broad API egress. If the same sensitive material is moved from Notion into RD-Agent, it can leave the workspace boundary and reach third-party APIs, creating an exfiltration path.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain confidential or regulated data and are forwarded into RD-Agent inputs, leakage is reachable.
IF RD-Agent processes those inputs through OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs, the data leaves local control.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive Notion pages into RD-Agent.
Redact secrets and personal data before any transfer.
Disable RD-Agent jobs on confidential datasets.
Review API destinations before each run.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP filters on Notion-to-RD-Agent exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and can act on workspace pages/databases; RD-Agent supports multiple instances, writes logs, and uses broad external APIs. Their mutable surfaces can overlap if both are pointed at the same project artifacts, creating write contention and inconsistent state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same shared project artifacts, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF RD-Agent writes logs or outputs that Notion later ingests, stale or partial state can be propagated.
mitigations: Assign separate folders or databases per agent.
Schedule runs so only one agent writes at a time.
Use read-only exports from Notion into RD-Agent.
Check for file/version conflicts before syncing.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and RD-Agent is an automation/research agent that can act on outputs via APIs and browser access. If RD-Agent consumes Notion-generated summaries or facts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The interaction is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Notion-generated summaries as authoritative inputs, mistaken facts can propagate.
IF RD-Agent then executes browser/API actions based on those facts, the error becomes operational.
mitigations: Require source links for every Notion-derived claim.
Have a human verify critical facts before RD-Agent acts.
Limit RD-Agent to drafting, not execution, on Notion-fed tasks.
Compare outputs against original workspace pages.
requires-engineering: add citation validation and action gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages under vendor-hosted backends, while RD-Agent can send financial reports, datasets, and logs to broad third-party APIs. If regulated or EU personal data moves from Notion into RD-Agent, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document a shared DPA, residency control, or aligned retention policy, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated records are copied from Notion into RD-Agent, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF RD-Agent routes those records to non-approved API providers, residency or retention controls may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent workflows.
Confirm approved regions and vendors before each run.
Minimize retention in both systems.
Document a data-processing basis for transfers.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
